answer: At dawn, an exchange hires agents to assess a zephyr-damaged trellis. Inspection slots are drawn by a verifiable random lottery weighted by each bidder’s locked stake, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across ten aliases leaves their combined winning chance at 100 divided by the total stake; each alias also pays a nonrefundable verification fee. An attacker must buy more stake to gain more slots, and false reports forfeit it. Wealthy bidders can dominate the lottery, so cap stake influence per audited funding source and reserve a share of slots for newcomers.
